text:
alex: Heads-up — saw a 99th-pct tail jump on Dedicated around 03:42 UTC. Profiling with nsys now. Early hypothesis: compile-queue saturation + kernel cache eviction during bursty batch patterns.

maria: Can you paste the nsys capture? Also did KV cache evictions show up in metrics?

alex: perf-bot posted the capture: /artifacts/nsys/1928001234-prod-spike.qdrep
Quick timeline summary: repeated triton_jit_compile ops ~60-120ms each, happening 6-8 times/sec during the spike. Kernel selector then falls back to a q-int8 conversion path with ~120ms overhead.

chen: That's odd — int8 fallback normally should be cheap. Are we compiling quant kernels on the fly?

alex: Yes. Sample from nsys timeline: 
``
0.120s triton_jit_compile kernel_name="matmul_qint" model=redwood-7b seq=1024
0.061s triton_jit_compile kernel_name="attn_qkv" model=redwood-7b seq=512
```
Those compile ops correlate exactly with RPC start times and tail latency spikes.

kyle: What about batching? Did heuristics create a high cardinality of batch keys?

alex: Exactly — batch key encodes (model, seq_len, kv_state). During the window we saw many small unique keys (1/3/5/16 mix) which prevented kernel reuse -> cold compiles.

rohit: Can we pre-warm by simulating the representative batch-key mix? Also precompile quant kernels for hot (model,seq) pairs?

maria: I ran a quick local sweep to measure compile times: 
``
model redwood-7b seq=512 q=fp16 compile=45ms
model redwood-7b seq=1024 q=int8 compile=118ms
model redwood-3b seq=1024 q=int8 compile=76ms
```

alex: If we precompile those hot permutations we can avoid the 2x-3x tail impact. Gotchas: compile cache size and eviction policy — we observed churn in /metrics/kernel_cache_evictions during the spike.

perf-bot: metric spike detected: kernel_cache_evictions=412 @1928001301; avg_compile_time=72ms

chen: Proposal: 1) change compile-key to ignore kv_state (bin by model_family + seq_len), 2) periodic precompile sweep covering model_family x seq_len distribution, 3) increase kernel cache capacity from 4k -> 16k entries on Dedicated.

kyle: Ignoring kv_state could be risky if kernels depend on KV layout. Need a compatibility test: ensure binary is agnostic to kv offset.

alex: We validated on staging: same kernel binary works across kv offsets for same dims. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/987 precomputes signatures and marks kernels as kv-agnostic for compile reuse.

rohit: Action items: alex upload nsys + perfetto links and a short runbook, maria run precompile sweep on canary, chen prototype compile-key change, kyle review binary compatibility. ETA: EOD tomorrow?

alex: Uploading nsys slices and a Perf note to #eng-runtime now. Also saw perfetto shows memcpy spikes right after compile completion — we copy kernels into device memory serially, creating short stalls. Parallelize uploads might help.

maria: +1. I'll run the precompile tonight on canary and post results.

kyle: If precompile reduces evictions we'll check memory impact. Also consider a tiny batching hold (5ms) to coalesce micro-batches and reduce unique keys.

chen: I'll spike an upload-thread-pool that parallelizes kernel device uploads.

perf-bot: nsys capture saved: s3://redwood-prod-traces/1928001234-prod-spike.qdrep
perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1928001234

rohit: Thanks all. Let's regroup at the weekly runtime sync. Will close this thread after patches land.
